management_steps.details: Peripheral (vestibular neuritis, labyrinthitis, BPPV): Sudden onset, severe, intermittent, horizontal unilateral nystagmus. Central (posterior stroke, cerebellar hemorrhage, tumor): Gradual/sudden, mild, continuous, purely vertical or direction-changing nystagmus, neurological deficits present.

management_steps.action: Apply HINTS bedside exam (for Acute Vestibular Syndrome)
management_steps.details: Rule out central cause: (1) Head Impulse Test (peripheral = catchup saccade, central = no saccade/normal - worrying!), (2) Nystagmus (peripheral = unilateral horizontal, central = direction-changing or vertical), (3) Test of Skew (central = refixation present after uncover, peripheral = no refixation).
BPPV: Dix-Hallpike maneuver to elicit nystagmus and confirm affected canal. Epley maneuver to reposition canaliths and resolve symptoms.
